hook_text: Two pizzas, different slices, one answer
clip_script:
Let us put the common denominator on a table. Two pizzas, same size. The first is cut into three slices and you take two of them: two thirds. The second is cut into four slices and you take three: three quarters. How much pizza do you have? You cannot say five slices of anything, because the slices are different sizes — a third of a pizza is bigger than a quarter. To add them you need to cut both pizzas into the same size slice.

Which slice size works? One that both thirds and quarters can be cut into exactly. Twelfths. Cut each third into four pieces: two thirds becomes eight twelfths. Cut each quarter into three pieces: three quarters becomes nine twelfths. Now every piece is a twelfth, and eight plus nine is seventeen twelfths.
visual_style: Overhead shot of two pizzas being re-cut into twelfths; chocolate-slab grid for multiplication
pacing: relaxed, with a beat as the slices line up
